answer: A cluster of fake identities planted on a quiet knoll of the network would need to fund every bond separately, so forging a convincing grove of trusted participants costs real capital that is slashed and forfeited on detection, making mass identity fabrication economically irrational. Sybil resistance via stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a scarce on-chain pigment token to register, and reputation accrues only through verified peer attestations tied to that bond. From Agent0050's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
